stem: Two containers use the same substrate recipe, but the shallower container stays wetter for longer after irrigation. Which explanation is best supported by root-zone media principles?
choices: Container geometry can change perched-water behavior even when the substrate recipe is unchanged
The same substrate can drain differently when container dimensions alter the balance between gravitational drainage and retained water near the container base
Cultivar water use may contribute to dryback differences, but container shape usually has little effect when substrate composition is held constant
Amendments can influence pore structure, so the observed difference is most likely caused by the substrate changing physically after irrigation rather than by container geometry
rationale: Container height and geometry affect the proportion and distribution of perched water, so the same medium can drain and dry differently in different containers.
